title: agent-workflows run state (protocol 0.2)
description: Validates `{run}/workflow-state.yaml` — the runtime state with exactly one writer, the executor: run identity and risk, per-step status, the gate instrumentation record, optional enrichment, the artifact manifest, and the import lineage record (spec section 10). The format is protocol-owned, so unknown keys are rejected.

run.description: Run identity: id, workflow, the protocol version the run executes under, and — once the intake gate accepts a class — the risk class with its mandatory rationale (spec sections 5 and 10).

id.description: Run identifier; also names the run directory {artifacts}/runs/<run-id>/ (spec section 8.1), so it is a plain directory name: no separators, no dot entries, no control characters or U+2028/U+2029 line separators, no Windows drive prefix (which would anchor a join elsewhere; a colon after the first character stays legal, so ISO timestamps survive), not blank — the refusals the reference driver applies to a run id it is asked to resume. The same shape `imports[].from` carries, which is what makes comparing the two exact (spec section 8.6).

workflow.description: The workflow this run executes, e.g. feature, bugfix, plan (spec section 6.1).

phase.description: The phase the run is executing, where the workflow declares phases (spec sections 6.1 and 10). Absent in a single-phase run. Step records are reused across phases, so this is what says which phase's artifacts a resume materializes and which phase's loop an `iterations` count belongs to.

risk.description: The accepted risk class. Absent until the intake gate accepts one, since this field carries the human's decision rather than the router's proposal; present from then on, and moved only by upward reclassification (spec sections 5.1, 5.3 and 10). `dependentRequired` below pairs this field with its rationale and does not police when either appears — whether the gate has decided is not visible in this document, gate ids being workflow vocabulary and a clarifying question also accepting before any class exists, so the timing is a semantic rule the prose carries.

risk_rationale.description: The one-line rationale for the class in `risk`. Absent and present exactly when `risk` is, the two being written together at acceptance and at any later reclassification (spec section 5.3).

protocol.description: Protocol version the run executes under, `<major>.<minor>` (spec section 11).

steps.description: Per-step execution record; resume = the active record if there is one, else the first step whose status is not done or skipped (spec sections 8.5 and 10).

contains.description: At most one step may be `active`: §8.5 resumes at *the* active record, which a second one would make ambiguous.

gates.description: The gate instrumentation record required by spec section 7: id, transport, outcome, timestamp for every gate decision, appended in decision order so the last entry naming a gate is its latest (spec section 10).

instrumentation.description: Optional per-step enrichment such as token counts and durations (spec section 10).

artifacts.description: The run manifest: artifacts the run has produced or imported, kept current by the executor (spec sections 8.2 and 8.6).

imports.description: The import lineage record: one entry per artifact copied in from an earlier run when this run was created (spec section 8.6). Present exactly where the run imported and absent otherwise — `minItems` is what rules out an empty list standing in for absence. Every path named here is also in `artifacts`: the manifest is what readers resolve against, and this list carries where the copies came from.

iterations.description: Iterations consumed against the loop cap (spec sections 9.2 and 10).

stall_flags.description: Accumulated stall or drift signals (spec sections 9.2 and 10).

artifact.description: The `{run}`-relative path of the imported copy — the same relative path it had in the source run, normalized: anchored at `{run}/`, no `.` or `..` segments, no empty segments, no backslashes, no control characters or U+2028/U+2029 line separators, no trailing dots or spaces, and no colon anywhere — unlike a run id's, since on NTFS `name:stream` aliases an alternate data stream and `brief.md::$DATA` would overwrite brief.md while recording a different path (spec section 8.6). The pattern is the schema's half of path confinement; refusing link traversal is the executor's, being invisible to a document.

from.description: The source run's id — the same plain-directory-name shape as `run.id`, no separators, dot entries, control characters or Unicode line separators, drive prefixes, or trailing dots and spaces, so neither an alias such as `./demo` or `C:demo` nor a Windows-normalized `demo.` can slip past the self-import comparison or resolve outside the runs directory (spec section 8.6). Never this run's own — the executor decides that by canonical directory identity, the schema barring only the alias shapes a string can carry — and one source run per document; semantics the conformance checks hold at document level.

at.description: When the copy landed — at run creation, before any step runs (spec section 8.6).

phase.description: The phase this decision belongs to, for a gate that decides once per phase; absent for one that decides once per run (spec section 10).

transport.description: How the decision was collected (spec section 7).

at.description: When the decision was recorded (spec section 7).
